3) Please share the procurement contact and any vendor form links (or let us know if procurement@fintechco.com is the right inbox).

- Our AP team requires vendor onboarding paperwork (W-9, bank remit instructions) and usually a vendor record before issuing POs. Will Redwood provide the documents for vendor setup?
- For PO flow: what billing cadence and terms do you require? Net 30 is our preference but need to confirm Redwood accepts that for new customers.
- Marketplace: if we go through AWS Marketplace is billing handled via AWS and faster for procurement? Any tradeoffs (e.g., feature parity, discounts)?

If you can send the SOW + vendor forms to procurement@fintechco.com I’ll route them to AP. Our tentative timeline: procurement aims to onboard new vendors by 6/25 if paperwork is received this week.

Thanks — I’ve attached the SOW template and our vendor onboarding checklist to this email (see attachments). Quick answers below: 

- Vendor documents: yes — we’ll provide W-9 and bank remit details and can complete Redwood’s onboarding questionnaire. I’ve attached the vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx which lists exactly what AP typically asks for.
- Billing/terms: Redwood supports Net 30 on PO-based billing for customers that sign SOW/MSA. We can accept a PO referencing the SOW and invoice monthly with Net 30. If you want to start immediately via credit card for a short pilot, we can do card billing and then transition to PO for production.
- Marketplace tradeoffs: AWS Marketplace can simplify procurement because billing goes through AWS, but there are timing/cost tradeoffs (AWS takes a cut and some contractual differences). Features are consistent for hosted API, but Dedicated/private deployments require separate contracts and cannot be purchased via marketplace today. 

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ll send the SOW + vendor checklist to procurement@fintechco.com (this thread copied).
2) If AP confirms they will issue a PO, let us know the PO target date and we’ll prepare an invoice and MSA/SOW for signatures (we can DocuSign both).
3) If AP prefers marketplace, I’ll introduce you to our partnerships lead and share the marketplace enrollment doc.

I’ll also loop in our solutions engineer for any technical acceptance criteria.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Alex — quick technical note from the SE side: 

- For a hosted API pilot (card or PO): no infra onboarding required. You get API keys scoped to the account and can restrict usage via rate limits and quotas.
- If you choose Dedicated or Private later (Reserved capacity or on-prem), that will require a separate SOW and vendor onboarding (we'll need MSA + technical onboarding window).
- Marketplace purchases are functionally the same for the hosted API, but if you want consolidated billing via AWS, we can provide guidance on the AWS Marketplace listing and catalog IDs.

If procurement needs a short acceptance checklist for the pilot, attach the vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx — it has the common items AP asks for. Happy to join a call with AP if they want to review technical controls.
